## Why Measuring Comes First (and Saves You Black Friday Returns)


Black Friday is almost upon us, and while the promise of massive discounts (especially for those who are quick to purchase) can be oh so tempting, here’s a reminder to pause and take a moment to assess what your pup really needs (or doesn’t need). That way, you’ll be prepared and won’t regret your purchase.


By knowing your[dog’s body size](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960982212001315?ref=petcube.com) and what to look out for when buying products for your dog, you avoid buying the wrong size, which can lead to discomfort, chafing, escaping, and the hassle of returning something your pup doesn’t need or that isn’t the right fit.


But where do you begin? When we talk about how to measure a dog, this often includes how to measure dog height as well as dog chest girth. In this article, we’ll cover how to measure your dog before you shop for dog clothing, gear,[equipment](https://petcube.com/blog/dog-training-tools/) , and accessories such as harnesses, collars, and coats. Get your soft tape measure,[treats](https://petcube.com/blog/healthy-treats/) , and a little help ready.


## How to Measure Your Dog: Height, Length, and Chest Girth


There are 3 core body measurements used for dog gear and clothing: neck girth, chest girth, and back length. Knowing these numbers lets you review sizing charts and pick the right size of clothing or gear for your dog.


When measuring your dog, keep them relaxed. Use treats or their favorite toy to help keep them still and make the process more comfortable for both of you.


### How to Measure Dog Chest Girth


Your dog’s chest girth is the circumference around the widest part of their rib cage. This measurement is often used to choose the right size of clothing or harness for your dog.


Tips:


1. With your dog standing, wrap the measuring tape around the widest part of their rib cage, usually just behind the front legs.
2. Make sure it’s snug without being too tight, and follow the two-finger rule for a comfy fit.


### How to Measure Dog Height or Length


Your dog’s back length, measured along their back or topline, is the measurement used to find the right length of clothing for your dog.


Tips:


1. With your dog standing up, measure along their spine from the base of the neck (where it joins the body) to the base of the tail.
2. For male dogs, choose clothing with a shorter cut around the belly to avoid accidents.


### How to Measure a Dog’s Neck


Your dog’s neck girth is the circumference of their neck, where their collar usually sits. It’s the measurement used to determine collar size, and it also matters when choosing harnesses and clothing. Getting the right fit makes sure your dog is comfortable and doesn’t feel restricted.


Tips:


1. Wrap the measuring tape around your dog’s neck where their collar sits. Start from the ridge between their shoulder blades, then wrap it around the front of the neck.
2. When you close the loop, use the two-finger rule to make sure there’s the right amount of space.


## Harness and Collar: How to Get the Fit Right


How do you measure a dog for a harness or collar?


### Two-Finger Rule


Like us humans, our pets don’t want to wear clothes that are too tight. To make sure there’s enough room for them to breathe, slip 2 fingers between your dog and the measuring tape when you measure their circumference.


### Neck vs. Chest


#### Harnesses


[Dr. Scott Miller, DVM](https://youtu.be/wD7vCDWwGRI?si=fczT1HEPDj3qnZvM&ref=petcube.com) , shares that a harness is a more comfortable alternative to a collar, as it shifts the pressure from the neck to the larger surface area of the chest and body.


There are different styles of harnesses, but they generally use the same measurements. To find the right size for your dog, their neck girth and chest girth matter most. Remember to follow the two-finger rule to leave breathing space.


#### Collars


How do you measure for a dog collar? For collars, you just need your dog’s neck measurement plus the two-finger rule. While most collars are adjustable, choosing the right size still helps your dog’s collar fit well and work as it should. For breeds with long necks, note that collars tend to sit on the upper part of the neck. Even so, it’s still recommended to measure the lower part of your dog’s neck, where standard collars usually rest.


**Tip:** When looking at the specifications of harnesses and collars, double-check the product’s sizing details. Some harnesses and collars are sized by a dog’s measurements, while others list the dimensions of the product itself. If your dog is between sizes, adjustable options are ideal. When adjustable options aren’t available, it’s better to go for a slightly bigger, slightly looser size rather than a smaller one.


## Puppies Outgrowing Gear


At what point do puppies outgrow their gear? In a Reddit[discussion](https://www.reddit.com/r/puppy101/s/xcSBhvWJec?ref=petcube.com) on r/puppy101, a pet parent with a 7-month-old puppy wondered when puppies outgrow their gear, as information online suggests that small breeds reach adult size around 6–10 months. One Redditor replied that her Pomeranian stopped growing at 8–9 months. In another Reddit[discussion](https://www.reddit.com/r/puppy101/s/FcMo5bswZQ?ref=petcube.com) , a Redditor gathered from various sources that puppies stop growing at around 12–18 months. A commenter noted that this may be true for larger breeds, but smaller breeds can finish growing as early as 6 months.[Here’s](https://petcube.com/blog/puppy-first-year/) an article to help you better understand puppy growth.


## What Size Crate Does Your Dog Need?


When it comes to[dog crate](https://petcube.com/blog/dog-crate-leaving/) size, the crate should be tall and long enough for your dog to comfortably stand up, turn around, and lie down. Adding at least 2–4 inches to their height and length is typically recommended. For[puppies](https://petcube.com/blog/raising-a-puppy/) , a crate with adjustable dividers can also help.


### Dog Crate Size: How to Measure Your Dog


- **Length:** Measure from the tip of your dog’s nose to the base of their tail, then add at least 2–4 inches.
- **Height:** Measure from the floor to the top of their head (or the tips of their ears if they stand upright), then add at least 2–4 inches.
- **Fit check:** When standing, your dog shouldn’t have to crouch or duck, and they should be able to stretch out when lying down.

## Winter Gear: Coats, Sweaters and Paw Boots


Not all dogs need winter gear, but some really do benefit from a little extra warmth.


So which dogs need a coat, and how do you measure a dog for clothes?


Short-haired breeds, small dogs, puppies,[senior dogs](https://petcube.com/blog/senior-dog-care/) , lean breeds (like Greyhounds), and dogs with health conditions may need a coat in[cold or wet weather](https://petcube.com/blog/winter-dog-care-gear-tips-and-tricks/) . If your dog[shivers](https://petcube.com/blog/when-is-dog-panting-abnormal/) or seems uncomfortable outside, it’s time to add a layer.


How to measure a dog for a coat or boots:


- **Back length:** Have your dog stand. Measure from the base of the neck (where the collar sits) to the base of the tail.
- **Paw size for boots:** To measure your dog’s paws, place each paw on a piece of paper while your dog is standing. Mark the widest points, then measure the paw’s width and length. Measure all four paws, as they can differ.


## After You Buy: Check How Your Dog Handles the New Gear


Monitor your dog and watch for signs such as rubbing,[stress in the crate](https://petcube.com/blog/dog-separation-anxiety/) , or[escape attempts](https://petcube.com/tracker/?ref=petcube.com) . Sometimes a product simply isn’t a good fit for your dog, or the size is wrong. A[Petcube Cam](https://petcube.com/cam/?ref=petcube.com) with the[Petcube App](https://petcube.com/mobile-app/?ref=petcube.com) lets you check how your dog settles into their new crate while you’re out, and how they like (or don’t like) their new gear. The app’s 24/7 vet chat is also there if you notice sore spots or chafing.


## Conclusion: Quick Size Cheat Sheet


Black Friday deals are exciting, but the best bargain is the one that fits your pup best. Before you hit the checkout button, grab your measuring tape, know where to measure, keep treats handy, and double-check the brand’s sizing chart. A little preparation prevents uncomfortable fits and spares you unnecessary returns (and money too!). And remember, your dog’s comfort should always come first.


**Quick Size Cheat Sheet**


- **Collar:** Neck circumference + two-finger allowance.
- **Harness:** Neck and chest girth + two-finger allowance.
- **Coat:** Back length, from neck base to tail base.
- **Boots:** Each paw’s length and width.
- **Crate:** Nose-to-tail length and floor-to-head height + 2–4 inches.


Finally, monitor your pup after introducing new gear. The right size isn’t just about looking good; it’s about keeping tails wagging!
